title: New Widget : autocomplete Select2 Js Library type
body:
the idea is to dispose of a widget able to search in a secondary index ( lets say an index of project for the sake of this example) with an autocomplete feature and a select2 kind of look. i think it should be pretty easy to build ?
maybe the issue is coming from the fact that the user need to be able to select a value (here a project) and then perform a new search in the real index ( which is a company listing that had worked on one or many projects)

comments.body:
Just to make sure I understand the issue, could you confirm this is the workflow you have in mind?
1. Users selects a project in a dropdown list (helped with an autocomplete so they do not have to scroll into the whole list).
2. Results are filtered, so only hits that matches this project are displayed
3. Users can type a query to further refine the list of results

In your example, the dropdown is populated through a secondary index, but this is actually used as a list of facets. How many projects (approx.) do you have in this list? Just to see if we're talking about a dropdown on a small list of facets, or a full search in another index.

Edit: Oh I just saw #401 where you've been asked to do a separate index. I guess this answers my question :)

my use case is as follows:
i have 36 000 projects linked to 40 000 companies.
Client requirement is to find companies that has worked on this or that project (with other facets also)

so i imagined the flow :
there is input allowing the user to search in the projet list. there is some kind of autocomplete or more likely a results list (capped to a maximum result i guess)
the user can click and select a project from the result list to add it to the search. Here companies results listing is refined
he can then search another projet and click and select it to add it to the search.Here companies results listing is refined
the 2 previous selected project should be easily removable as well.

EDIT: just saw your edit :)

As of today, I think you could be able to build something like this using our [autocomplete.js](https://github.com/algolia/autocomplete.js) library (this is a fork of Typeahead that uses Algolia) and the `instantsearch.helper` property (that maps to our [javascript helper](https://github.com/algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js).

This will require a bit of plumbing, but the main idea would be to listen to the `autocomplete:selected` event of `autocomplete.js`, and here add a new `facetRefinement` to the `helper`, that matches the value selected in `autocomplete`...

We have plans to add search into facets values directly at the API level, but no ETA at the moment. I don't think we're going to add this feature like this directly into instantsearch core (because of file size, and custom setup requirements in term of indices), but maybe we should write a detailed guide on how our two libraries could work together.

Any other thoughts @redox @vvo @bobylito ?

We could definitely create a community widget that given the user as the right configuration would provide a refinementList sort widget with an input search on top of it and custom behavior to add remove refinements.

Would that work?
:+1: From my POV, this would work. It only requires a bit of specific index configuration on the user side. But we could explain all that in this widget specific readme.

> We could definitely create a community widget that given the user as the right configuration would provide a refinementList sort widget with an input search on top this is not really like select2...
Indeed @bobylito, we have two different widgets here (that's why a GIF/screenshot is worth 6 github comments :D).

@chrisvidal There's no current implementation of what you really want. If you want to go further on creating a specific widget, I would advise you to:
- build a graphical mockup of the widget (how would it look in a simple way)
- list the features available for the user
- design a JavaScript API listing the widget options

Then once you have all this design setup we can walk you through internal implementation.

You can do so in a new issue, it will be easier.

Thanks a lot!
now the tricky part i guess, is to link the object named 'client' in the helpers which look like an instance of the old algolia search with the new 'serachclient' coming from the instantsearch API

@chrisvidal
- "algoliasearch" is the JS API client (just handling requests to the API).
- The helper (algoliasearch-helper) is the search state holder (what are the current refinements/query). It wraps the algoliasearch client
- instantsearch is then wrapping helper

If you have a test repository I can have a look and help you out.

I am wondering though, how is this `select2`?
The title here might be a "tad" off, because select2 is [this](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/issues/757#issuecomment-170935298), would get populated by whatever values come from `attribute`, and instead of being a "simple" select, it is... a select2 select instance.

I do not see how the solutions herein proposed solve any of this?
